text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA)

PUA provides unemployment benefits to claimants who are not working as a result of COVID-19 and are self-employed, independent contractors, gig economy workers, and others who otherwise would not qualify for regular UC or Extended Benefits under state or federal law or Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation (PEUC). PUA benefits start at $267 per week but may be higher based on the earnings in the tax year before the client applied.

UI Online displays limited information about the PUA income type. Procedures for verifying PUA are found later in this document under Verifying PUA Income.

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation (PEUC)

The PEUC program provides extended unemployment insurance benefits to claimants who have exhausted their previous unemployment benefits. PEUC claimants will be identified in the Current Program column in the Weeks Claimed section of the claimant’s UI Online profile. It will be displayed as PEUC.

metadata.page_title: Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Federal Pandemic Unemployment Compensation (FPUC)

This benefit provides an additional $300 per week to individuals who are collecting regular Unemployment Compensation (UC), Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation (PEUC), Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA), Extended Benefits (EB), Trade Readjustment Act (TRA), or Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DA).

FPUC will be paid at $300 per week and can be seen on UI Online under the Additions column. It will be displayed as FPUC when you click the Week End Date.

Important: This income is not countable for SNAP and TAFDC and must not be added to the client’s weekly unemployment benefit amount.

metadata.page_title: Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Mixed Earner Unemployment Compensation (MEUC)

Mixed Earner Unemployment Compensation payments are a type of Federal Pandemic Unemployment Compensation (FPUC) payment authorized under Sec. 2104 of the CARES Act. MEUC payments are an additional $100 per week available to individuals that currently receive certain types of unemployment compensation. In addition, the individual must have received a net income of at least $5,000 in self-employment in the past year and received wages (not from self-employment). Clients receiving Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) are ineligible for MEUC.

MEUC is not countable for SNAP or TAFDC and must not be added to the client’s weekly unemployment benefit amount. You must write a detailed narrative stating that the client is receiving MEUC, including the weekly amount, frequency, and that it is noncountable. An update will be provided when more information is available about how this benefit type will or will not display on UI Online.

metadata.page_title: Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types

Effective for week ending September 4, 2021 all Pandemic Unemployment Compensation types are terminated. This includes:

- Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA)
- Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation (PEUC)
- Federal Pandemic Unemployment Compensation (FPUC)
- Mixed Earner Unemployment Compensation (MEUC)

A batch job will go into each active case currently receiving a type of pandemic unemployment, remove the income, and recalculate the case automatically. A batch narrative will also be entered that the case was recalculated. Additionally, a standard EBC notice will go out to clients to notify them of their benefit change. Clients who do not have Heightened Level of Security HLS) or have not opted-out of text messaging, will also receive a DTA Text Alert notifying them that the Department is working with DUA to remove the income and that they do not need to do anything.

metadata.page_title: Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income
metadata.section_heading: Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Application – SNAP

If a client is applying for SNAP and was previously receiving unemployment compensation and it has ended, you must count any terminated unemployment compensation that falls within the client’s initial cyclical month, by verifying the payment date amounts displayed on UI Online. Entering and processing unemployment compensation is outlined in Unemployment Compensation . Y ou must enter and calculate all terminated income as monthly in BEACON. You must create a follow-up action to go in the next day to end the terminated unemployment income and wrap the case for ongoing benefits.

If a client applies for SNAP and it is determined that they will have terminated unemployment income, but the last unemployment benefit check (the week of 9/6/21) has not yet been issued, you must use the same amount the client previously received the week prior as the income amount to be added to the client’s total terminated income amount.

metadata.page_title: Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income
metadata.section_heading: Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Application – SNAP
metadata.parent_heading: Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Application – SNAP

Example Example Shiloh’s SSN ends in a 0. She applies for SNAP on 9/1/21. She reports that she has been receiving $267/week in PUA benefits, but it is going to end on 9/4/21. Shiloh will be receiving her last check for the last claim date of 9/4/21 sometime the week of 9/6/21. (Typically, UI benefits are paid on Tuesdays or Wednesdays). Her cyclical is 9/1 - 9/30. This means Shiloh’s 9/1/21 PUA benefit and her upcoming 9/8/21 PUA benefit must be counted as terminated income. You must add the $267 benefit amount Shiloh previously received on 9/1/21 to the additional $267 PUA benefit she will receive the week on 9/8/21. Her total terminated income amount will be $534. Remember to create a follow-up action to go in the next day once the initial month’s benefit is released to remove the terminated income for ongoing.

Remember: All types of unemployment compensation that have ended for a client near the application date (including Regular UI) must always be considered as terminated income, if applicable.

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Application – SNAP

You must always use the payment date when entering any type of Unemployment Compensation type in BEACON. For procedures regarding how to find and enter the payment date, please see Unemployment Compensation .

Important: The PUA benefit section on UI Online already identifies the payment date.

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Application – TAFDC

If a client is applying for TAFDC and was previously receiving unemployment compensation and it has been ended, you must not count any terminated income. The case manager must end the income in BEACON and move the effective date of the application to the date after the last unemployment compensation payment was received.

You must follow up once the first month’s benefits are released to remove the terminated income from being counted in the ongoing calculation of SNAP benefits.

metadata.parent_heading: Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Recertification and Ongoing – SNAP

If a case is active, the batch will automatically remove any Pandemic Unemployment Compensation types and recalculate the case.

When processing Recertifications for October, the Pandemic Unemployment Compensation types must be ended in BEACON and noted in the narrative.

Terminated Income is no longer counted during Recertification.

If the Household’s Net Income Drops to Zero the Month of September Due to Removing the Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Type - SNAP

If a client reports that their Pandemic Unemployment Compensation type has ended, you must remove the income. Once you have removed the income, you must determine if their household’s net income is reduced to zero. If the household’s net income has reduced to zero, you must issue a related benefit for the month of September. Additionally, you must also issue a related benefit for the $95 base SNAP Emergency Allotment for the month of September. You must use the client’s September cyclical month start and end dates for both the September supplement and the Emergency Allotment supplement when entering the amounts in the Related Benefit window in BEACON.

metadata.section_heading: Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Recertification and Ongoing – SNAP
metadata.parent_heading: Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Termination of All Pandemic Unemployment Compensation Types > Termination of Pandemic Unemployment Compensation at Recertification and Ongoing – SNAP

For clients whose Pandemic Unemployment Compensation types are being removed by the automated batch process, a review will be done to issue these clients a related benefit, if applicable.

Remember: If a household’s net income does not reduce to zero for the month of September once the Pandemic Unemployment benefits are removed, do not issue a supplement for the September Emergency Allotment. Clients will still be made whole through the SNAP Emergency Allotment batch process. For more information regarding SNAP Emergency Allotments, click here .

text:
COVID-19 > Processing Cases with Pandemic UC Income > Overpayment Referrals - SNAP

If a client failed to report PUA income at application or recertification an overpayment referral (UPV) must made.

If a client failed to report receipt of PUA benefits while their SNAP case was active, and the amount exceeded their gross income limit, the case manager must complete an overpayment referral and mark the referral as a UPV.

For all Active SNAP and EA clients with PUA or PEUC amounts in the DUA batch job file, and where there is no unemployment record in BEACON, the batch will automatically create an Overpayment Referral. A batch narrative will be generated stating, “Batch Referral – Confirm Unemployment Income Not Previously Known to BEACON.”
